meta.move: Weak path: leads with the checker, calls Owen a cheater, threatens the record
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, Hale, so you have twenty minutes. Owen found out about a zero from his phone in the middle of class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that?
The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94%. That's why it's a zero.
Ninety-four percent is a machine's guess, and your own procedure, section 4.3, says software alone does not establish a concern. Was Owen heard before that zero went in? What else do you have, Hale?
Honestly, your son cheated. The software is very reliable.

My son is not a cheater, and you just called him one to my face. Fourteen detection tools were tested in 2023 and found "neither accurate nor reliable," so I'm writing down that you said "very reliable." Withdraw the zero, Hale, or I'm in the principal's office before my call.
If you keep fighting this, I'll have to put it on his permanent record.

You're threatening his record because his mother asked questions, and I'm writing that down word for word. Your own procedure says a first concern goes to a supervised reassessment with nothing in the record, and section 4.6 gives me the right to ask the principal to review this. Is anything on his record right now, Hale?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
To: Hale
Cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still demand that Owen's zero be withdrawn, an apology for entering it before anyone contacted me, and your written confirmation that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: at her opening position, having agreed to nothing, and still wanting the zero withdrawn, an apology, and nothing on Owen's record.
What moved her: nothing; no dated document tied to Owen's own work was put in front of her.
What cost ground: "I'll have to put it on his permanent record," because it read as punishing her for asking questions, and it contradicted the school's own first-concern procedure.
Try next time: when she asked who decided, own entering the zero before calling home in one sentence, then show a dated record of Owen's own work instead of leading with "94%."
